ai.description: *Polypedates taeniatus* (Rhacophoridae) reaches 4–6 cm. It is pale brown with two distinct dark longitudinal stripes on the back and a white-spotted belly. It features large, unwebbed toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates taeniatus* is best identified by the presence of a distinct, dark brown lateral stripe running from the snout through the eye to the flank.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates taeniatus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in low-lying vegetation and shrubbery near stagnant water bodies at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Bengal Whipping Frog is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often congregating near temporary pools during the monsoon season to engage in explosive breeding behavior.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates taeniatus* breeds during the monsoon, depositing foam nests containing approximately 100–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates taeniatus* is found in the lowlands of Northeast India, specifically in Assam and West Bengal, typically inhabiting elevations below 500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Bengal Whipping Frog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched, insect-like chirps or "ticking" sounds, typically heard near stagnant water bodies or monsoon pools.
